clue.text: Bedroom chats about being out of action

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of the two words beside it are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Pillow talk that leaves someone too worn out to do anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges BEDROOM CHATS; 'being' is a link. HORS DE COMBAT is a French phrase borrowed into English.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase literally means outside the fight, used of a soldier or player disabled and unable to take part.

clue.text: Spiral shaped lilac given to ambassador

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title used for an ambassador

indicators.note: shaped means the word lilac is formed into a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A flower arrangement in a twisting form presented to a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spiral shaped' reads as one adjective, but 'shaped' is the anagram signal working on LILAC, giving LICAL; 'given to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something helical winds round like a coil or screw thread, which is a spiral form.

clue.text: Checks concerned with fashionable crime

parts.note: RE is the Latin-derived word for about or regarding, as in a letter heading
IN means trendy or fashionable
a sin is a wrongdoing, loosely a crime

explanation.surface: Inspections looking into a trendy kind of wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in a horse or a spending habit is to restrain or curb it, a verb sense of checks.

clue.text: Ruthless boxers welcome feed

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the dogs enclose the next piece

parts.note: boxers are a breed of dog; the plural gives two of them, DOG and DOG
to feed is to eat

explanation.surface: Unsparing fighters greet a meal being served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxers' looks like pugilists, but it means the dog breed; two dogs take in EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-eat-dog world is one of cut-throat competition where everyone is merciless.

clue.text: Trainee soldier from America detained

indicators.note: from tells the solver the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A young recruit is held by the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'America' and the start of 'detained'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a young person training to become an officer in the armed forces.

clue.text: Lame — but can be changed

indicators.note: can be changed tells us the letters of the two words beside it are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is lame, but the condition need not be permanent.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the letters of LAME BUT can be changed into a word meaning able to be changed.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutable means liable to alter or variable, the opposite of fixed.

clue.text: A weak attorney finds a way through the trees

parts.note: lame means weak or feeble, as in a lame excuse
DA is the American abbreviation for district attorney

explanation.surface: A feeble lawyer discovers a woodland path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finds' is a link. An ALAMEDA, from Spanish, is a public walk shaded by trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish-derived word names a promenade or avenue lined with poplars or other trees.

clue.text: Still at home? Good! Put some clothes on, but what to wear?

parts.note: even means still, as in still better or even better
IN means at home
to dress is to put clothes on

explanation.surface: Someone lounging at home is told to get dressed but cannot decide on an outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link; the definition is the final question, read as a cryptic hint at formal attire.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening dress is formal clothing for night-time occasions, so it is something to wear.

clue.text: Putting a price on a liberal university (fashionable) in very good surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the abbreviation for very good encloses the other pieces

parts.note: VG is the abbreviation for very good, as on a school report
IN means trendy or fashionable

explanation.surface: An appraisal of a trendy liberal college set in pleasant grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' before 'very good' is a link; 'surroundings' puts A, L, U and IN inside V and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Valuing an item means estimating its worth, that is, pricing it.

clue.text: Leave the coach having been instructed to promote the last two

indicators.note: the last two names the final pair of letters, each of which is moved up in turn
to promote is to move up a rank, so a letter from the end goes to the front of the word

parts.note: trained means taught or instructed

explanation.surface: Someone gets off the bus after being told to move two people up a ranking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to promote' and 'the last two' move the final pair of TRAINED to the front one at a time: E first gives ETRAIND, then D gives DETRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To detrain is to get off a railway carriage, and coach is a word for such a carriage.

clue.text: Affluent oriental supporting new French upstart

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means placed underneath the piece named after it

parts.note: nouveau is the French word for new
affluent means rich
E, for east, is the usual abbreviation for oriental

explanation.surface: A wealthy man from the East backs a fresh French social climber.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'supporting' puts RICH and E beneath NOUVEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase describes someone who has newly acquired wealth and flaunts it, a social upstart.

clue.text: Provincial firm's first class return for capital

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is often called the Province
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm; the possessive gives CO'S

indicators.note: return means the letters for first class are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first class, written with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: A regional company's premium service offers a refund in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provincial' looks like an ordinary adjective, but Northern Ireland is known as the Province. First class is A1, written with the letter I for the one; 'return' reverses it, and 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the chief city and seat of government of Cyprus.

clue.text: A dramatic scene — the board get gold!

parts.note: a board is a table, as in bed and board
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: The company directors celebrate getting a gold award in theatrical fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is a link. AU comes from the Latin aurum.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking group of people arranged as in a picture, often on stage.

clue.text: Company at last invested in new look with new fabric

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, as money is placed in a venture

parts.note: LO is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A firm finally puts money into a fresh image with a novel material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes Y from 'Company'; 'invested in' places it inside N + LO; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer made into cloth, stockings and thread.

clue.text: Criticise decrease in value without one

indicators.note: without means the letter for one is left out

parts.note: to depreciate is to lose value
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Complaining about a falling price when someone is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes I from DEPRECIATE. The two words are often confused, which makes the clue neat.
explanation.definitionFit: To deprecate is to express disapproval of something, which is to censure it.

clue.text: Portion the food bit by bit?

parts.note: a piece is a portion
a meal is food eaten at one sitting

explanation.surface: Doling out a serving of food in small instalments.
explanation.definitionFit: Done piecemeal means done gradually, in stages rather than all at once.

clue.text: Rabble-rouser who expected to welcome oriental giant

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the first piece encloses the others

parts.note: due means expected, as in the train is due
E, for east, is the usual abbreviation for oriental
Magog is one of the legendary giants Gog and Magog

explanation.surface: An agitator who was supposed to greet a huge visitor from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who' is a link. Gog and Magog are legendary giants whose figures stand in London's Guildhall.
explanation.definitionFit: A demagogue is a political agitator who sways crowds by appealing to emotion and prejudice.

clue.text: Refusal to support holy city with this building material

indicators.note: in a down answer, to support means to sit underneath the piece named after it

parts.note: Mecca is the holy city of Islam
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A rejection of a sacred site's plans for using certain materials.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'to support' puts NO below MECCA. MECCANO is a metal construction toy of strips, nuts and bolts; 'with this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The construction kit of perforated metal strips is used by children to assemble models.

clue.text: Tearing out from hard rock!

indicators.note: out means the letters of the word before it are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone rips something away from a solid stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tearing out' reads as ripping, but 'out' scrambles TEARING; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Granite is a coarse-grained igneous stone, notably tough.

clue.text: Unhappy hour, oddly, for an ascetic

parts.note: unhappy means sad

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and so on letters of the word

explanation.surface: A miserable sixty minutes for a hermit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps H and U from 'hour'; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sadhu is a Hindu holy man who has renounced worldly life, an ascetic.

clue.text: Almost be ill, eating one cold — that will be enough

indicators.note: eating means the first piece takes the others inside it
almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to suffer is to be ill or in pain
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone feeling poorly eats a single chilly item and declares that sufficient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims SUFFER to SUFFE; 'eating' puts I and C inside it. 'that will' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffice is to be adequate or meet a need.

clue.text: Agreements to protect province result in rejections

indicators.note: to protect is to surround, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: deals are agreements
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called the Province

explanation.surface: Treaties to safeguard a region end in refusals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result in' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Denials are refusals, statements saying no or disowning something.

clue.text: The Vatican perhaps achieved clean break with victory in Europe

indicators.note: break means the letters of the word clean are smashed into a new order

parts.note: VE stands for victory in Europe, as in VE Day

explanation.surface: The Holy See won a clean break when the war in Europe ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges CLEAN to ENCLA; 'achieved' and 'with' are links. 'perhaps' marks the Vatican as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a territory entirely surrounded by another state, as Vatican City is by Rome and Italy.

clue.text: Surplus old paintings put up

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: in a down answer, put up means the word is written upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: art is paintings collectively

explanation.surface: Spare old pictures are hung on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like hanging pictures on a wall, but in a down entry it means the word is written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional or more than needed, which is surplus.

clue.text: Finish in fife, poor but with honourable title

indicators.note: in means the word for finish is placed inside the other piece
poor means the letters of fife are badly arranged

parts.note: an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A poverty-stricken ending in a Scottish county, yet with a grand title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' makes EFFI, an anagram of the printed word, and 'in' puts the word for finish inside it. Fife is a Scottish county; 'but with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi was a Turkish term of respect for a man of education or standing, like sir.

clue.text: View lost, we hear, due to fog

indicators.note: we hear means the words before it are said out loud to give a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to see is to view and lost is missed, giving see missed

explanation.surface: The scenery has vanished because of a thick fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'due to' is a link. SEE MISSED said aloud sounds like a coastal haze.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea mist is a fog rolling in from the sea over the coast.

clue.text: Inscription from old record — it needs a quiet hour!

parts.note: EP, extended play, is an old record format
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: An old single needs a short peaceful spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' and 'needs' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is words carved on a tombstone in memory of the dead.

clue.text: All upset over badly-knitted jumpers

indicators.note: badly-knitted says the letters of the three words before it are put together in a jumbled way

explanation.surface: Everyone is disappointed about some poorly made sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' looks like knitwear to match 'badly-knitted', but it means athletes; 'badly-knitted' rearranges ALL UPSET OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Pole vaulters are athletes who leap over a high bar using a long flexible pole.
